description: GRADED mutant catalog — teacher-only, deliberately kept outside the student's spec-test-driven/ folder so neither a learner nor their agent can read which cases matter. Superset of the visible practice catalog: it adds the subtle accessory-matching defects that separate a thorough suite from a merely green one, plus two spec-dependent mutants whose survival is acceptable. Regenerate with ./gradlew generateMutants in THIS build; score a suite with ./gradlew verifyMutants -PmutantTests=<learner|authored|path> --continue.

mutants.find: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = duck.hasKotlinAttribute
mutants.replace: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = true
mutants.what: KotlinOnly ignores the attribute and admits every duck.
mutants.hint: a negative-direction test — a duck WITHOUT the Kotlin attribute is rejected

mutants.find: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = duck.price <= maxPrice
mutants.replace: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = duck.price < maxPrice
mutants.what: MaxBudget rejects a duck priced exactly at the limit (strict instead of inclusive).
mutants.hint: a boundary test — a duck whose price equals the limit is admitted

mutants.find: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = duck.accessories.size >= min
mutants.replace: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = duck.accessories.size > min
mutants.what: MinAccessories rejects a duck wearing exactly the minimum number of accessories.
mutants.hint: a boundary test — exactly `min` accessories is enough

mutants.find: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = duck.accessories.any { it.name == accessoryName }
mutants.replace: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = duck.accessories.any { it.name.startsWith(accessoryName) }
mutants.what: RequiresAccessory matches any accessory whose name merely STARTS WITH the required one.
mutants.hint: an exact-name test — a duck wearing only a "hatband" does not satisfy RequiresAccessory("hat")

mutants.find: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = duck.accessories.any { it.name == accessoryName }
mutants.replace: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = duck.accessories.firstOrNull()?.name == accessoryName
mutants.what: RequiresAccessory only looks at the FIRST accessory instead of all of them.
mutants.hint: a test where the matching accessory is not the first one in the list

mutants.find: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = duck.accessories.any { it.name == accessoryName }
mutants.replace: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = duck.accessories.any { it.name.equals(accessoryName, ignoreCase = true) }
mutants.hint: a case-sensitivity test — "HAT" does not satisfy RequiresAccessory("hat")

mutants.find: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = policies.all { it.admits(duck) }
mutants.replace: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = policies.isNotEmpty() && policies.all { it.admits(duck) }
mutants.what: AllOf over an empty list rejects every duck instead of admitting them (vacuous truth lost).
mutants.hint: a vacuous-truth test — AllOf(emptyList()) admits any duck

mutants.find: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = policies.any { it.admits(duck) }
mutants.replace: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = policies.isEmpty() || policies.any { it.admits(duck) }
mutants.what: AnyOf over an empty list admits every duck instead of rejecting them.
mutants.hint: a vacuous-truth test — AnyOf(emptyList()) admits nobody

mutants.find: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = policies.all { it.admits(duck) }
mutants.replace: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = policies.any { it.admits(duck) }
mutants.what: AllOf behaves like OR: one satisfied policy is enough.
mutants.hint: a test where exactly one of several policies says no and AllOf must reject

mutants.find: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = policies.any { it.admits(duck) }
mutants.replace: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = policies.all { it.admits(duck) }
mutants.what: AnyOf behaves like AND: every policy has to agree.
mutants.hint: a test where exactly one of several policies says yes and AnyOf must admit

mutants.replace: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = policy.admits(duck)
mutants.what: Not forwards the wrapped decision instead of inverting it — the defect planted in the starter suite.
mutants.hint: a test that Not really inverts, in both directions

mutants.find: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = policies.all { it.admits(duck) }
mutants.replace: override fun admits(duck: Duck): Boolean = policies.map { it.admits(duck) }.all { it }
mutants.what: AllOf evaluates every policy instead of stopping at the first rejection — same answers, no short-circuit.
mutants.hint: only a spy policy counting its own calls can tell the difference; the spec never promises short-circuiting

mutants.find: class AllOf(private val policies: List<AdmissionPolicy>) : AdmissionPolicy {
mutants.replace:
class AllOf(policies: List<AdmissionPolicy>) : AdmissionPolicy {
    private val policies: List<AdmissionPolicy> = policies.toList()
mutants.what: AllOf copies the list it is given, so mutating that list afterwards no longer changes the policy.
mutants.hint: only a test that mutates the caller's list after construction can tell; the spec is silent — this is the under-specification the exercise asks about
